claims.evidence: This is a comparison to previous studies, supported by citations.

claims.claim: The absence of HCO3- permeability in Slc26a9T contrasts with some reports showing evidence of Cl-/HCO3- exchange.
claims.source: However, the absence of HCO3– permeability is in contrast to some reports showing evidence of Cl–/HCO3– exchange by Slc26a9 which were based on measurements of intracellular pH changes in response to removal of external Cl– in the presence of bath HCO3– (Chang et al., 2009b; Xu et al., 2005).
claims.evidence: This is a comparison to previous studies, supported by citations.

claims.claim: All reports of electrogenic transport by Slc26a9 indicate negligible movement of HCO3-.
claims.source: While we cannot fully account for this discrepancy we note that all reports of electrogenic transport indicate negligible movement of HCO3–.
claims.evidence: This is a statement about the consensus in the literature.

claims.claim: The conductivity sequence of Slc26a9T is Cl->Br->NO3-~SCN->I-.
claims.source: To assess relative transport rates, macroscopic conductance ratios (Gx/GCl) of permeable anions revealed a conductivity sequence of Cl–>Br– > NO3–~SCN–>I– (Figure 1F; Figure 1—figure supplement 3B,C).
claims.evidence: This is supported by conductance ratio measurements from bi-ionic substitution experiments.

claims.claim: The conductivity pattern of Slc26a9T deviates from the permeability sequence, with Cl- being considerably more conductive than any other tested anion.
claims.source: Notably, the conductivity pattern deviates from the permeability sequence, with Cl– being considerably more conductive than any other tested anion.
claims.evidence: This is observed from comparing permeability and conductance data.

claims.claim: The high relative permeability of lyotropic anions shows that they face a lower energy barrier for dehydration and entry into the transport pathway compared with Cl-.
claims.source: The high relative permeability of lyotropic anions shows that they face a lower energy barrier for dehydration and entry into the transport pathway compared with Cl–, while their lower relative conductance implies that they also encounter a deeper energy well, which in turn would decrease their overall turnover rate.
claims.evidence: This is an interpretation of the permeability and conductance data.

claims.claim: Lyotropic anions encounter a deeper energy well in Slc26a9T, which decreases their overall turnover rate.
claims.source: The high relative permeability of lyotropic anions shows that they face a lower energy barrier for dehydration and entry into the transport pathway compared with Cl–, while their lower relative conductance implies that they also encounter a deeper energy well, which in turn would decrease their overall turnover rate.
claims.evidence: This is an interpretation of the permeability and conductance data.

claims.claim: SCN- has a lower Km and Vmax compared to Cl- in Slc26a9T.
claims.source: These properties are also reflected in the lower Km and Vmax of SCN– compared to Cl– (Figure 1D) and suggest that Slc26a9 has evolved as an efficient uncoupled Cl– transporter.
claims.evidence: This is supported by conductance-concentration relationship data.

claims.claim: Slc26a9 has evolved as an efficient uncoupled Cl- transporter.
claims.source: These properties are also reflected in the lower Km and Vmax of SCN– compared to Cl– (Figure 1D) and suggest that Slc26a9 has evolved as an efficient uncoupled Cl– transporter.
claims.evidence: This is inferred from the functional properties observed.

claims.claim: The structure of Slc26a9T was determined by cryo-EM at 3.96 Å resolution in detergent.
claims.source: A 3.96 Å dataset of Slc26a9T purified in the synthetic digitonin analogue glyco-diosgenin (GDN) was of high quality and allowed the unambiguous interpretation of the cryo-EM density by an atomic model (Figure 2; Figure 2—figure supplements 1 and 2; Table 1; Video 1).
claims.evidence: This is supported by cryo-EM data and model refinement statistics.

claims.claim: The structure of Slc26a9T was determined in lipid nanodiscs at 7.77 Å resolution.
claims.source: To exclude a possible bias from a detergent environment, we have in parallel reconstituted the purified protein into lipid nanodiscs and determined its structure at low (7.77 Å) resolution (Figure 2—figure supplements 3 and 4; Video 2).
claims.evidence: This is supported by cryo-EM data from nanodisc-reconstituted protein.

claims.claim: Both detergent and nanodisc datasets display similar general features of the protein with respect to the organization of subunits and their oligomeric arrangement.
claims.source: Both datasets display similar general features of the protein with respect to the organization of subunits and their oligomeric arrangement, although the nanodisc structure reveals localized rigid-body movements indicative of a different functional conformation.
claims.evidence: This is observed from comparing the two cryo-EM structures.

claims.claim: The nanodisc structure reveals localized rigid-body movements indicative of a different functional conformation.
claims.source: Both datasets display similar general features of the protein with respect to the organization of subunits and their oligomeric arrangement, although the nanodisc structure reveals localized rigid-body movements indicative of a different functional conformation.
claims.evidence: This is observed from comparing the two cryo-EM structures.

claims.claim: Slc26a9T is a dimer of elongated shape that is approximately 100 Å long and 50 Å wide.
claims.source: The protein is a dimer of elongated shape that is approximately 100 Å long and 50 Å wide (Video 3).
claims.evidence: This is observed from the cryo-EM structure.

claims.claim: The STAS domains of Slc26a9T protrude 38 Å into the cytosol.
claims.source: The interacting domain-swapped STAS domains, appearing as a knob centered on one side of Slc26a9T particles, protrude 38 Å into the cytosol, while a spiky loop on each subunit projects towards the extracellular solution (Figure 2; Figure 2—figure supplements 1–4).
claims.evidence: This is observed from the cryo-EM structure.

claims.claim: The interactions between both subunits of the dimeric Slc26a9T are highly unusual since they only exhibit minimal contacts between the membrane-inserted domains.
claims.source: The interactions between both subunits of the dimeric protein are highly unusual since, unlike other proteins with a similar fold, they only exhibit minimal contacts between the membrane–inserted domains at the intracellular end of the last transmembrane helix (Figure 2).
claims.evidence: This is observed from the cryo-EM structure and comparison to other proteins.

claims.claim: Only 11% of the buried surface in the Slc26a9T dimer can be attributed to interactions directly between the transmembrane domains.
claims.source: Of the 8'114 Å2 of the combined molecular surface buried in the dimer, only 11% can be attributed to interactions directly between the transmembrane domains (TMDs).
claims.evidence: This is calculated from the cryo-EM structure.

claims.claim: 16% of the buried surface in the Slc26a9T dimer is contributed by mutual contacts between STAS domains.
claims.source: Conversely, 16% of the buried surface is contributed by mutual contacts between STAS domains whereas the remaining interactions are mutually formed between the swapped STAS domain and the transmembrane part of the opposing subunit.
claims.evidence: This is calculated from the cryo-EM structure.

claims.claim: The extended N-terminus of Slc26a9T binds to the STAS domain and appears to contribute to dimer stability.
claims.source: Another remarkable feature of the dimer interface concerns the binding of the extended N-terminus to the STAS domain, which appears to contribute to dimer stability (Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
claims.evidence: This is observed from the cryo-EM structure.

claims.claim: In the Slc26a9T dimer, the cytoplasmic STAS domains act as a platform for interactions between subunits.
claims.source: In the Slc26a9T dimer, the cytoplasmic STAS domains act as a platform for interactions between subunits, thus explaining the deleterious transport phenotype observed upon mutations or its removal in different family members (Babu et al., 2010; Dorwart et al., 2008a; Geertsma et al., 2015; Sharma et al., 2011) (Figure 3, Video 3).
claims.evidence: This is observed from the cryo-EM structure and supported by citations to previous functional studies.

claims.claim: The STAS domain of Slc26a9T closely resembles known STAS domain structures from eukaryotic SLC26A5 (Prestin) and the bacterial homolog SLC26Dg.
claims.source: This cytoplasmic unit closely resembles known STAS domain structures from eukaryotic SLC26A5 (Prestin) (Lolli et al., 2016; Pasqualetto et al., 2010) and the bacterial homolog SLC26Dg (Geertsma et al., 2015) (Figure 3—figure supplement 2A,B).
claims.evidence: This is observed from structural comparison.

claims.claim: The STAS domain consists of a six-stranded mixed β-sheet core decorated with four interspersed α-helices.
claims.source: It consists of a six-stranded mixed β-sheet core, which is decorated with four interspersed α-helices (Figure 1—figure supplement 1 and Figure 3—figure supplement 2A).
claims.evidence: This is observed from the cryo-EM structure.

claims.claim: Several loop regions of the STAS domain make contacts with the TMD of the opposing subunit at parts close to the membrane.
claims.source: Several of the loop regions connecting β-strands with their adjoining α-helices (i.e. the β3-Cα1, β4-Cα2, β5-Cα3 and the Cα3-β6 loops) make contacts between the STAS domains and the TMD of the opposing subunit at parts that are close to the membrane (at the α4-α5, α8-α9, α12- α13 loops and the terminal helix α14) (Figure 3).
claims.evidence: This is observed from the cryo-EM structure.

claims.claim: The strong conservation of residues at the contact region between STAS and TMD points towards the preservation of this interface among family members.
claims.source: The strong conservation of residues at the contact region with the TMD points towards the preservation of this interface among family members (Figure 1—figure supplement 1A and Figure 3—figure supplement 2C).
claims.evidence: This is inferred from sequence alignment and structural analysis.

claims.claim: At the bottom part of the STAS dimer, interactions with the N-terminus are mediated by the β1-β2, β2-β3 and β6-Cα4 loops.
claims.source: At the bottom part of the STAS dimer, interactions with the N-terminus are mediated by the β1-β2, β2-β3 and β6-Cα4 loops (Figure 3—figure supplement 2D).
claims.evidence: This is observed from the cryo-EM structure.

claims.claim: A negatively charged groove at the dimer interface of the STAS domain could potentially interact with cellular factors.
claims.source: Between both regions, on the side of the STAS dimer, a negatively charged groove at the dimer interface could potentially interact with cellular factors (Figure 3—figure supplement 2E,F).
claims.evidence: This is inferred from structural analysis showing a charged surface.

claims.claim: In the dimeric architecture of the STAS domain, the two unstructured regions removed in Slc26a9T would be located opposite to the dimer-interface and thus be available for interactions with accessory proteins.
claims.source: Finally, in the observed dimeric architecture of the STAS domain, the two unstructured regions removed in the Slc26a9T construct would be located opposite to the dimer-interface and thus be available for interactions with accessory proteins (Figure 3—figure supplement 2G).
claims.evidence: This is inferred from the structure of the truncated construct.

claims.claim: The overall architecture of the TMD conforms to the 7+7 inverted repeat topology.
claims.source: The overall architecture of the TMD conforms to the 7 + 7 inverted repeat topology (Figure 1—figure supplement 1 and Figure 4—figure supplement 1), which was previously observed in the structure of the prokaryotic homologue SLC26Dg (Geertsma et al., 2015) and in members of the distantly related SLC4 (Arakawa et al., 2015; Huynh et al., 2018) and SLC23 (Alguel et al., 2016; Lu et al., 2011) families.
claims.evidence: This is observed from the cryo-EM structure and comparison to other structures.

claims.claim: The Slc26a9T TMD is composed of 14 membrane-inserted α-helices, with α8-14 representing a similar yet inverted organization to α1-7.
claims.source: Consistent with the known features of this arrangement, the Slc26a9T TMD is composed of 14 membrane-inserted α-helices, with α8–14 representing a similar yet inverted organization to α1–7 (Figure 4—figure supplement 1).
claims.evidence: This is observed from the cryo-EM structure.

claims.claim: The TMD is segregated into two subdomains: a convex core module (consisting of α1-4 and 9-11) carrying a putative ion-binding site, and a concave gate module (consisting of α5-7 and 12-14).
claims.source: The TMD is segregated into two subdomains, a convex core module (consisting of α1–4, and 9–11) carrying a putative ion-binding site, and a concave gate module (consisting of α5–7 and 12–14) (Figure 4, Video 3).
claims.evidence: This is observed from the cryo-EM structure.

claims.claim: Both core and gate modules constitute independent structural units that interact via an extended interface.
claims.source: Both modules constitute independent structural units that interact via an extended interface (Figure 4A).
claims.evidence: This is observed from the cryo-EM structure.

claims.claim: The TMD of Slc26a9T shows a high degree of similarity to its equivalent unit of SLC26Dg (RMSD of 2.0 Å).
claims.source: Although displaying channel-like functional properties, the structure of the TMD of Slc26a9T shows hallmarks of a transporter. The striking degree of similarity revealed from a superposition with its equivalent unit of SLC26Dg (RMSD of 2.0 Å) emphasizes the high conservation within the family and suggests that both structures display equivalent conformations (Figure 5A–C).
claims.evidence: This is observed from structural superposition.

claims.claim: The large cavity between gate and core modules is accessible from the intracellular side but does not extend into a contiguous pore region towards the extracellular side.
claims.source: The large cavity between gate and core modules is accessible from the intracellular side but does not extend into a contiguous pore region towards the extracellular side, suggesting that the Slc26a9T structure represents an inward-open state of the protein that facilitates transport by an alternate-access mechanism.
claims.evidence: This is observed from the cryo-EM structure.

claims.claim: The Slc26a9T structure in detergent represents an inward-open state of the protein.
claims.source: The large cavity between gate and core modules is accessible from the intracellular side but does not extend into a contiguous pore region towards the extracellular side, suggesting that the Slc26a9T structure represents an inward-open state of the protein that facilitates transport by an alternate-access mechanism.
claims.evidence: This is inferred from structural features.

claims.claim: The nanodisc TMD structure differs from the detergent structure in the conformation of the core module, which has rotated by approximately 14° and moved by 4 Å towards the extracellular side.
claims.source: This assumption is further supported by the comparison of TMDs of Slc26a9T from cryo-EM maps acquired either in detergent micelles or lipid nanodiscs (Figure 2—figure supplement 4C–E). The nanodisc TMD structure differs in the conformation of the core module, which has rotated as rigid body by approximately 14° and moved by 4 Å towards the extracellular side, whereas the remainder of the protein appears largely unaltered.
claims.evidence: This is observed from comparing the two cryo-EM structures.

claims.claim: The nanodisc structure likely shows an intermediate state of the protein on its transition towards an outward-facing state.
claims.source: This conformation thus likely shows an intermediate state of the protein on its transition towards an outward-facing state (Figure 5D; Video 4).
claims.evidence: This is inferred from comparing the detergent and nanodisc structures.

claims.claim: A loop-helix structure connecting α5-α6 (α5') fills a depression in the structure created by the short α13-α14 turn.
claims.source: First, a loop-helix structure connecting α5-α6 (α5') fills a depression in the structure created by the short α13–α14 turn, which would not otherwise reach the boundary of the outer leaflet of an undistorted bilayer (Figures 4B and 5B).
claims.evidence: This is observed from the cryo-EM structure.

claims.claim: The loop region connecting α3 and the extended α4 protrudes into the extracellular space and contains two predicted glycosylation sites near the tip.
claims.source: A second distinguishing feature of Slc26a9T concerns the loop region connecting α3 and the extended α4, which protrudes into the extracellular space and which contains two predicted glycosylation sites (Li et al., 2014) near the tip of the spiky extension (Figures 4C and 5C).
claims.evidence: This is observed from the cryo-EM structure and supported by a citation about glycosylation sites.

claims.claim: The extended N-terminus of Slc26a9T is significantly longer than the equivalent region in SLC26Dg.
claims.source: Finally, the extended N-terminus of Slc26a9T, preceding α1, is significantly longer than the equivalent region in SLC26Dg (Figure 5C).
claims.evidence: This is observed from structural comparison.

claims.claim: The N-terminus of Slc26a9T is partly mobile and contains extended regions with interspersed secondary structure elements.
claims.source: In the mammalian transporter, the N-terminus is partly mobile and contains extended regions with interspersed secondary structure elements.
claims.evidence: This is observed from the cryo-EM structure.

claims.claim: A structured part of the N-terminus preceding α1 forms scattered helical segments peripherally contacting the inner membrane leaflet and containing several basic residues.
claims.source: Whereas the initial part of the N-terminus engages in the earlier described interaction with the STAS domains, a mobile linker bridges this region to a structured part preceding α1, which forms scattered helical segments peripherally contacting the inner membrane leaflet and containing several basic residues (Figure 5C, bottom inset).
claims.evidence: This is observed from the cryo-EM structure.

claims.claim: Due to high sequence conservation between paralogs, the three structural features (α5', extracellular loop, extended N-terminus) are likely preserved in mammalian SLC26 transporters.
claims.source: Due to the high sequence conservation between paralogs (Figure 1—figure supplement 1A), all three structural features are likely preserved in mammalian SLC26 transporters.
claims.evidence: This is inferred from sequence conservation.

claims.claim: In the inward-facing conformation, transported anions enter the protein via a wide aqueous vestibule, attracted by positive electrostatic potential from basic amino acids at its intracellular entrance.
claims.source: In the observed inward-facing conformation of the TMD, transported anions enter the protein to access their binding site via a wide aqueous vestibule, presumably attracted by the positive electrostatic potential that is conferred by an excess of basic amino acids at its intracellular entrance (Figure 6A,B).
claims.evidence: This is observed from the structure and supported by electrostatic calculations.

claims.claim: For wild-type Slc26a9T, the linear I-V relationship is compatible with symmetric rate-limiting barriers on the transport cycle in the absence of applied voltage.
claims.source: For wild-type (WT) Slc26a9T, the linear I-V relationship is compatible with symmetric rate-limiting barriers on the transport cycle in the absence of applied voltage (Lam and Dutzler, 2018; Paulino et al., 2017).
claims.evidence: This is inferred from the I-V relationship and supported by citations.

claims.claim: Mutations R205E or K358E minimally perturb the linear I-V relationship of Slc26a9T.
claims.source: This linear relation is minimally perturbed upon introducing the mutations R205E or K358E, which are positioned at the outermost regions of the intracellular vestibule (Figure 6A; Figure 6—figure supplement 1A).
claims.evidence: This is supported by electrophysiology data on mutants.

claims.claim: Mutations K270E and K443E, located deeper in the intracellular cavity, display considerable outward rectification.
claims.source: In contrast, mutations K270E and K443E, located deeper in the intracellular cavity and close to the presumed anion binding site, both altered the electrostatics and displayed considerable outward rectification (Figure 6A–C).
claims.evidence: This is supported by electrophysiology data on mutants.

claims.claim: The outward rectification in K270E and K443E mutants indicates a relative increase of the inward barrier.
claims.source: This behavior indicates a relative increase of the inward barrier by either impeding the access of anions from the intracellular side or alternatively by hampering conformational transitions of the protein.
claims.evidence: This is inferred from the electrophysiology data.

claims.claim: Mutation of extracellular basic residues K221 and K431 leads to inward rectification.
claims.source: Complimentary to the intracellular charge-reversal mutations, we find a reciprocal effect leading to inward rectification upon mutation of extracellular basic residues K221 and K431 that are predicted to line the aqueous cavity to the binding site in an outward-facing conformation (Figure 6—figure supplement 1B,C).
claims.evidence: This is supported by electrophysiology data on mutants.

claims.claim: An anion binding site is inferred to be located in a pocket of the core domain between the N-termini of the membrane-inserted partial helices α3 and α10.
claims.source: Although in our cryo-EM reconstructions we did not observe any density attributable to bound Cl–, its absence is concordant with its measured low apparent affinity. We infer an anion binding site to be located in a pocket of the core domain between the N-termini of the membrane-inserted partial helices α3 and α10 (Figures 4C and 7A; Video 5).
claims.evidence: This is inferred from structural analysis and comparison to related transporters.

claims.claim: The equivalent location to the inferred Slc26a9 binding site was proposed as a substrate-binding site for the fumarate-proton symporter SLC26Dg and the chloride-bicarbonate transporter SLC4A1/Band 3.
claims.source: The equivalent location was proposed as a substrate-binding site for the fumarate-proton symporter SLC26Dg (Chang et al., 2019a) and the chloride-bicarbonate transporter SLC4A1/Band 3 (Arakawa et al., 2015) and confirmed for the SLC23 transporters UraA (Lu et al., 2011) and UapA (Alguel et al., 2016).
claims.evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claims.claim: The binding site is ideally positioned at the apex of the inward-open cavity, with dual pseudo-symmetrically related helix dipoles arranged in a manner frequently observed for binding sites of anion transporters.
claims.source: This site would be ideally positioned at the apex of the inward-open cavity, with its dual pseudo-symmetrically related helix dipoles arranged in a manner frequently observed for binding sites of anion transporters (Dutzler et al., 2002; Screpanti and Hunte, 2007) (Figures 4C and 7A).
claims.evidence: This is observed from structural analysis and supported by citations.

claims.claim: Compared to SLC26Dg, the pocket of Slc26a9T is considerably smaller due to the conformation of F128 projecting its side-chain into the pocket.
claims.source: Compared to SLC26Dg, the pocket of Slc26a9T is considerably smaller, as a consequence of the conformation of F128 projecting its side-chain into the pocket, thus creating a site of appropriate size for a Cl– ion (Figure 7A).
claims.evidence: This is observed from structural comparison.

claims.claim: Residues F128, F92, and L391 contribute to the partly hydrophobic character of the binding site, which likely accounts for the observed lyotropic permeability sequence of anions.
claims.source: In this site, several residues could plausibly interact with the transported substrates. Besides F128, these include the nonpolar residues F92 and L391, all contributing to the partly hydrophobic character frequently found in anion binding sites which likely account for the observed lyotropic permeability sequence of anions (Figure 1E) (Dani et al., 1983; Dutzler et al., 2002).
claims.evidence: This is inferred from structural analysis and supported by citations.

claims.claim: Dehydrated anions could be stabilized by side-chain interactions with Q88, S392, and possibly T127, as well as main-chain interactions at the N-terminus of α10.
claims.source: Dehydrated anions could be stabilized by side-chain interactions with Q88, S392, and possibly T127, as well as main-chain interactions at the N-terminus of α10, which together form a cradle to coordinate the desolvated ion (Figure 7A).
claims.evidence: This is inferred from structural analysis.

claims.claim: Several binding-site mutants altered the linear I-V relationship, with S392A showing inward rectification and F128A and Q88A showing outward rectification.
claims.source: To probe the functional importance of potential binding-site residues for anion interactions, we individually mutated them to alanine and used inside-out patch recordings to assess any corresponding changes in transport behavior (Figure 7—figure supplement 1A–G). Several mutants altered the linear I-V relationship, with the resulting inward rectification of the mutant S392A indicating a relative increase of the outer barrier and conversely, the outward rectification in the mutants F128A and Q88A, a relative increase of the inner barrier during transport (Figure 7B, Figure 7—figure supplement 1A,D,F).
claims.evidence: This is supported by electrophysiology data on mutants.

claims.claim: Only minor perturbations of the linear I-V relationship are found for the binding site residues F92A and L391A.
claims.source: In contrast, only minor perturbations of the linear I–V relationship are found for the binding site residues F92A and L391A and no change is observed for the mutant N441A residing on the gate module, which, although proximal to the site, is not predicted to participate in ion coordination (Figure 7—figure supplement 1B,E,G).
claims.evidence: This is supported by electrophysiology data on mutants.

claims.claim: The mutant Q88E shows severely decreased currents that are strongly outward-rectifying, consistent with compromised transport activity due to interference of the negatively charged residue with transported anions.
claims.source: The change in the conductance properties upon mutation of Gln 88 is even more pronounced in the mutant Q88E, which replaces the amino acid conserved in mammalian paralogs with a negatively charged residue found in several prokaryotic transporters (Geertsma et al., 2015). Despite the strong apparent surface expression and high stability of the mutant, there are no currents observed in excised patches and severely decreased currents in whole-cell measurements are strongly outward-rectifying, consistent with a compromised transport activity due to the interference of the negatively charged residue with the transported anions (Figure 7—figure supplement 1H,I).
claims.evidence: This is supported by electrophysiology data on the mutant.

claims.claim: Changes in the inverted relationship between permeability and conductivity are most pronounced for S392A and F128A, where chloride becomes less conductive than other permeant anions.
claims.source: Although affected in all binding-site mutants (Figure 7—figure supplements 2 and 3A–E; Table 2), changes are most pronounced for S392A and F128A, where chloride becomes less conductive than other permeant anions, a behavior that is also reflected in the kinetic parameters obtained from the concentration dependence of transport of Cl– and SCN– (Figure 7C–H; Figure 7—figure supplement 3; Table 2).
claims.evidence: This is supported by bi-ionic substitution and conductance-concentration data on mutants.

claims.claim: The mutant L391A shows a pronounced increase in the Km of SCN- by nearly two orders of magnitude.
claims.source: A pronounced difference is also observed for the mutant L391A where the Km of SCN– increases by nearly two orders of magnitude (Figure 7—figure supplement 3I; Table 2).
claims.evidence: This is supported by conductance-concentration data on the mutant.

claims.claim: In no case did binding-site mutants show major increases in permeation by either HCO3- or SO42-, nor evidence of coupled transport.
claims.source: Whereas the strong effect of different binding-site mutants on conduction underlines their importance for anion transport, in no case did we detect major increases in permeation by either HCO3– or SO42–, nor did we observe any evidence of coupled transport (Figure 7—figure supplements 1A–G and 2; Table 2).
claims.evidence: This is supported by bi-ionic substitution data on mutants.

claims.claim: The dimeric organization of Slc26a9 differs markedly from structurally related transport proteins of the SLC4 and SLC23 families, which interact via an extended interface between gate modules.
claims.source: The dimeric organization of Slc26a9 differs markedly from structurally related transport proteins of the SLC4 and SLC23 families, which interact via an extended interface between gate modules (Alguel et al., 2016; Arakawa et al., 2015; Chang and Geertsma, 2017; Huynh et al., 2018; Yu et al., 2017) (Figure 8—figure supplement 1).
claims.evidence: This is observed from structural comparison and supported by citations.

claims.claim: In Slc26a9, the interface between the TMDs is minimal whereas the bulk of subunit interactions are mediated by the cytoplasmic STAS domains involving contacts with the N-terminus and intracellular loop regions of the gate module.
claims.source: In contrast, in Slc26a9 the interface between the TMDs is minimal whereas the bulk of subunit interactions are mediated by the cytoplasmic STAS domains involving contacts with the N-terminus and intracellular loop regions of the gate module (Figure 2).
claims.evidence: This is observed from the cryo-EM structure.

claims.claim: A similar minimal contact relationship between transmembrane domains was recently proposed to underlie dimerization of the prokaryotic transporter SLC26Dg in a membrane environment, based on EPR-derived distance constraints.
claims.source: A similar relationship between transmembrane domains was recently proposed to underlie dimerization of the prokaryotic transporter SLC26Dg in a membrane environment, based on EPR-derived distance constraints (Chang et al., 2019b).
claims.evidence: This is supported by a citation to a previous study.

claims.claim: Minimal contacts in the membrane-inserted domain have been recently observed for the mechanosensitive channel OSCA, where subunit interactions are mediated exclusively between residues of the cytoplasmic domains.
claims.source: Although such minimal contacts in the membrane-inserted domain are unusual for oligomeric membrane proteins, they have been recently observed for the mechanosensitive channel OSCA (Jojoa-Cruz et al., 2018; Zhang et al., 2018), where subunit interactions are mediated exclusively between residues of the cytoplasmic domains.
claims.evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claims.claim: Slc26a9 shows large uncoupled macroscopic Cl- currents that saturate only at high mM concentration.
claims.source: As previously shown based on whole-cell experiments (Bertrand et al., 2009; Chang et al., 2009b; Dorwart et al., 2007; Loriol et al., 2008) and confirmed here with excised patches, Slc26a9 shows large uncoupled macroscopic Cl– currents that saturate only at high mM concentration.
claims.evidence: This is supported by electrophysiology data and citations.

claims.claim: The properties of Slc26a9 would be entirely consistent with a fast bidirectional uniport mechanism.
claims.source: For this reason, the protein has been generally referred to as ion channel. However, such properties would be entirely consistent with a fast bidirectional uniport mechanism as evidenced by other structural and functional data shown in our study.
claims.evidence: This is inferred from the functional and structural data.

claims.claim: The high Km of Cl- matches its intracellular concentration and would foster high turnover leading to the observed conduction phenotype.
claims.source: The high Km of Cl– matches its intracellular concentration and would foster high turnover leading to the observed conduction phenotype.
claims.evidence: This is inferred from the measured Km and physiological Cl- concentrations.

claims.claim: Transport of the hydrophobic ion SCN- saturates at lower concentration consistent with a mechanism mediated by an anion binding site.
claims.source: Moreover, transport of the hydrophobic ion SCN– saturates at lower concentration consistent with a mechanism that is mediated by an anion binding site, which would be expected in a transporter.
claims.evidence: This is inferred from the measured Km for SCN-.

claims.claim: Structural data clearly suggest that Slc26a9 works by an alternate-access mechanism akin to other family members.
claims.source: Additionally, our structural data clearly suggest that Slc26a9 works by an alternate-access mechanism akin to other family members.
claims.evidence: This is inferred from the structural data showing different conformations.

claims.claim: The inward-facing structure of Slc26a9T shows the ion binding site accessible to the cytoplasm.
claims.source: This is evidenced by a comparison between the inward-facing structure of Slc26a9T determined in detergent, where the ion binding site is accessible to the cytoplasm, and an intermediate conformation of the lipid nanodisc-reconstituted transporter, where an upward movement of the core module has caused the binding site to be buried between core and gate modules (Figure 8A,B).
claims.evidence: This is observed from the cryo-EM structure.

claims.claim: In the intermediate conformation, an upward movement of the core module has caused the binding site to be buried between core and gate modules.
claims.source: This is evidenced by a comparison between the inward-facing structure of Slc26a9T determined in detergent, where the ion binding site is accessible to the cytoplasm, and an intermediate conformation of the lipid nanodisc-reconstituted transporter, where an upward movement of the core module has caused the binding site to be buried between core and gate modules (Figure 8A,B).
claims.evidence: This is observed from the cryo-EM structure.

claims.claim: Both structures provide insight into conformational changes in which the relatively unconstrained core module makes ascending and descending rigid-body movements relative to the immobilized gate module-STAS domain complex, in a process that resembles the elevator transport mechanism.
claims.source: In combination, both structures provide insight into conformational changes in which the relatively unconstrained core module, providing the substrate binding site, makes ascending and descending rigid-body movements relative to the immobilized gate module-STAS domain complex, in a process that resembles the elevator transport mechanism (Drew and Boudker, 2016; Ficici et al., 2017; Reyes et al., 2009) (Figure 8B).
claims.evidence: This is inferred from comparing the two structures and supported by citations.

claims.claim: Such an elevator-like mechanism would allow for fast transport kinetics as observed for Slc26a9T and as previously described for the Cl-/HCO3- transporter SLC4A1/Band 3.
claims.source: Such mechanism would allow for fast transport kinetics as observed here and as previously described for the Cl–/HCO3– transporter SLC4A1/Band 3, which shares a similar architecture (Arakawa et al., 2015; Brahm, 1977).
claims.evidence: This is inferred from the structural mechanism and supported by citations.

claims.claim: The plausible homology to the known outward-facing structure of SLC4A1/Band 3 permits the anticipation of the possible extent of conformational changes in Slc26a9.
claims.source: The plausible homology to the known outward-facing structure of SLC4A1/Band 3 (Arakawa et al., 2015) also permits the anticipation of the possible extent of conformational changes, where basic residues on the rim of the resulting extracellular vestibule likely create a positive electrostatic environment which is similar to that observed in the vestibule of the inward-facing state.
claims.evidence: This is inferred from structural homology and supported by a citation.

claims.claim: The role of electrostatics in the transport mechanism is supported by functional experiments and model-based calculations.
claims.source: The role of electrostatics in this hypothesis is supported by functional experiments and model-based calculations (Figure 6A–C; Figure 6—figure supplement 1).
claims.evidence: This is supported by mutagenesis data and Poisson-Boltzmann calculations.

claims.claim: During transport, the negatively charged Cl- is dragged across the transmembrane electric field, thus likely facilitating conformational changes.
claims.source: During transport, the negatively charged Cl– is dragged across the transmembrane electric field, thus likely facilitating conformational changes.
claims.evidence: This is inferred from the electrostatic properties and transport mechanism.

claims.claim: A similar mechanism may underlie the substrate-conferred electromotility observed in the homologous motor protein Prestin.
claims.source: A similar mechanism may underlie the substrate-conferred electromotility observed in the homologous motor protein Prestin (Oliver et al., 2001).
claims.evidence: This is speculated based on the mechanism observed for Slc26a9 and supported by a citation.

claims.claim: The inability of Slc26a9 to transport SO42- is probably related to the fact that interactions within the binding site may not be sufficiently strong for the coordination of divalent anions.
claims.source: The lyotropic permeability sequence of Slc26a9 suggests that ions interact with a low field-strength binding site. The inability to transport SO42– is thus probably related to the fact that interactions within the binding site, which does not contain positive countercharges to balance the negatively-charged substrate, may not be sufficiently strong for the coordination of divalent anions.
claims.evidence: This is inferred from the structural and functional properties.

claims.claim: All other mammalian SLC26 family members harbor very similar predicted binding sites to that of Slc26a9, with the notable exception that they additionally contain a positively charged amino acid at the equivalent position of V393.
claims.source: Remarkably, all other mammalian family members harbor very similar predicted binding sites to that of Slc26a9, with the notable exception that they additionally contain a positively charged amino acid at the equivalent position of V393, which is located on the N-terminal end of helix α10 (Figure 8C; Figure 8—figure supplement 2).
claims.evidence: This is observed from homology models and sequence alignment.

claims.claim: Homology models predict the positively charged side-chain at the equivalent position of V393 to reside very close to the substrate binding site in other mammalian SLC26 paralogs.
claims.source: Homology models predict this side-chain to reside very close to the substrate binding site (Figure 8—figure supplement 2), and an arginine at the equivalent location, which likely contributes to anion interactions, is also found in the Cl–/HCO3– transporter SLC4A1/Band 3 (Arakawa et al., 2015) (Figure 8C).
claims.evidence: This is observed from homology models and supported by a citation.

claims.claim: The inability of Slc26a9 to transport HCO3- is particularly remarkable, since the nearly isosteric molecular anion NO3- is a transported substrate.
claims.source: The inability of Slc26a9 to transport HCO3– is particularly remarkable, since the nearly isosteric molecular anion NO3– is a transported substrate (Figure 1E).
claims.evidence: This is observed from the functional data.

claims.claim: The equilibrium between HCO3- and CO32- could be perturbed at the binding site, with the large positive electrostatic potential stabilizing the divalent state of the ion, for which interactions with the anion binding site would not be sufficiently strong.
claims.source: Although the pKa for the deprotonation of HCO3– is high (i.e. 10.3) and consequently the concentration of the divalent anion CO32– is negligible under physiological conditions, the equilibrium could be perturbed at the binding site, with the large positive electrostatic potential within the aqueous cavity stabilizing the divalent state of the ion, for which interactions with the anion binding site would not be sufficiently strong to make it a transported substrate.
claims.evidence: This is speculated based on the electrostatic properties and binding site characteristics.

claims.claim: The high homology between mammalian SLC26 paralogs suggests a common general architecture.
claims.source: The high homology between mammalian SLC26 paralogs suggests a common general architecture and also implies that other family members may undergo similar conformational transitions to those shown here for Slc26a9T.
claims.evidence: This is inferred from sequence conservation.

claims.claim: Other SLC26 family members may undergo similar conformational transitions to those shown for Slc26a9T.
claims.source: The high homology between mammalian SLC26 paralogs suggests a common general architecture and also implies that other family members may undergo similar conformational transitions to those shown here for Slc26a9T.
claims.evidence: This is inferred from sequence conservation and structural similarity.

claims.claim: The diversity of functional phenotypes in the SLC26 family could rely on comparatively small localized structural differences which impose variable energy barriers for conformational changes.
claims.source: Therefore, the diversity of functional phenotypes ranging from uncoupled bidirectional uniport as observed in Slc26a9 (and possibly SLC26A7 and/or SLC26A11), to coupled exchangers such as SLC26A2/DTDST and SLC26A4/Pendrin, or even to the motor activity of SLC26A5/Prestin (Alper and Sharma, 2013), could rely on comparatively small localized structural differences which in turn impose variable energy barriers for conformational changes (Figure 8—figure supplement 3).
claims.evidence: This is speculated based on the structural and functional diversity.

claims.claim: Uncoupled uniporters like Slc26a9 presumably possess small conformational energy barriers between inward and outward states in the presence or absence of substrate which would permit transition of an unloaded transporter.
claims.source: Uncoupled uniporters like Slc26a9 presumably possess small conformational energy barriers between inward and outward states in the presence or absence of substrate which would permit transition of an unloaded transporter.
claims.evidence: This is speculated based on the observed mechanism.

claims.claim: For coupled transport, the presumed increase in ion binding affinity paired with an enlarged barrier prohibiting conformational transitions of the unloaded transport domain would itself lead to stoichiometric exchange.
claims.source: In contrast, for coupled transport the presumed increase in ion binding affinity paired with an enlarged barrier prohibiting conformational transitions of the unloaded transport domain would itself lead to stoichiometric exchange.
claims.evidence: This is speculated based on mechanistic principles.

claims.claim: The electromotile motor function of SLC26A5/Prestin could be a consequence of an insurmountable energy barrier preventing the last phase of the transition to an outward-facing state.
claims.source: In this view, the electromotile motor function of SLC26A5/Prestin could be a consequence of an insurmountable energy barrier preventing the last phase of the transition to an outward-facing state, in line with prior suggestions of SLC26A5/Prestin exhibiting an 'incomplete' transport cycle (Schaechinger and Oliver, 2007).
claims.evidence: This is speculated based on the mechanism and supported by a citation.

claims.claim: Electrophysiology experiments show instantaneous activity of Slc26a9T that is not obviously dependent on activating ligands.
claims.source: Since our electrophysiology experiments show instantaneous activity of the transporter that is not obviously dependent on activating ligands (Figure 1B), the question concerning the regulation of Slc26a9 activity under physiological conditions is pertinent.
claims.evidence: This is observed from electrophysiology data.

claims.claim: A potential activation mechanism could be the mobilization of SLC26A9 from intracellular stores, which might be regulated by phosphorylation.
claims.source: A potential activation mechanism could be the mobilization of SLC26A9 from intracellular stores, which might be regulated by phosphorylation, as suggested in a previous study (Dorwart et al., 2007) and which is also consistent with the predominantly intracellular localization of full-length Slc26a9 observed in our study (Figure 1—figure supplement 2A).
claims.evidence: This is speculated based on previous studies and the observed localization.

claims.claim: The IVS may harbor modifiable motif elements which can be involved in surface-trafficking regulation.
claims.source: The fact that removal of the IVS results in significantly greater surface expression suggests that this region may harbor modifiable motif elements which can be involved in surface-trafficking regulation, but this hypothesis must be further evaluated in more physiologically relevant contexts.
claims.evidence: This is speculated based on the observed effect of IVS deletion.

results.result: The truncated construct Slc26a9T (lacking IVS and CT regions) exhibits greater surface expression, can be purified to homogeneity as a dimer, and retains robust Cl- transport activity that can be inhibited by DIDS. The IVS region appears responsible for intracellular retention of full-length Slc26a9, and the purified protein does not require cellular factors for activity.
results.evaluation: Claims C27-C32 are well-supported by fluorescence microscopy (C27), comparison of truncation constructs (C28), size-exclusion chromatography (C29), and fluorometric transport assays (C30-C31). The inference that Slc26a9T does not require cellular factors (C32) is directly supported by observing activity in reconstituted proteoliposomes. The data consistently demonstrate that the truncation strategy successfully produced a functional, well-behaved protein suitable for structural and functional studies.

results.result: Slc26a9T exhibits constitutively active, anion-selective currents with linear I-V relationships in both whole-cell and inside-out patch configurations. Currents are at least 4-fold larger than full-length Slc26a9, reverse at the Cl- Nernst potential (indicating Cl- is the only transported charge), and show saturation at high Cl- concentrations with a Km of 30 mM. No single-channel transitions were observed.
results.evaluation: Claims C33-C39 are strongly supported by comprehensive electrophysiology data from whole-cell and inside-out patch-clamp recordings. The reversal potential measurements under various ionic gradients (C37) directly support the conclusion that Cl- is the only transported charge (C38). The Km determination (C39) is based on conductance-concentration relationships. The negative result regarding single-channel transitions (C36) contrasts with one previous study but is clearly stated as an observation from the current experiments.

results.result: Slc26a9T displays a lyotropic permeability sequence (SCN->I->Br->NO3->Cl-) but negligible permeability for F-, HCO3-, and SO42-. The conductivity sequence (Cl->Br->NO3-~SCN->I-) deviates from the permeability sequence, with Cl- being considerably more conductive than other anions. This pattern suggests Slc26a9 has evolved as an efficient uncoupled Cl- transporter, with lyotropic anions facing lower dehydration barriers but deeper energy wells that decrease turnover.
results.evaluation: Claims C41-C51 are well-supported by systematic bi-ionic substitution experiments and conductance measurements. The permeability sequence (C41) and negligible permeabilities for certain anions (C42) are directly measured. The comparison to previous studies (C43-C45) appropriately contextualizes the findings. The mechanistic interpretations about energy barriers and wells (C48-C49) are reasonable inferences from the permeability and conductance data. The conclusion that Slc26a9 is an efficient Cl- transporter (C51) is supported by the kinetic parameters.

results.result: The structure of Slc26a9T was determined by cryo-EM at 3.96 Å resolution in detergent and at 7.77 Å resolution in lipid nanodiscs. Both datasets show similar overall organization of subunits and oligomeric arrangement, though the nanodisc structure reveals localized rigid-body movements indicative of a different functional conformation.
results.evaluation: Claims C52-C55 are supported by the cryo-EM data collection and processing described in the methods and results. The resolutions are appropriate for the conclusions drawn, with the detergent structure at near-atomic resolution allowing detailed model building, and the lower-resolution nanodisc structure sufficient to observe conformational differences. The comparison between the two structures (C54-C55) is directly observable from the structural data and provides important validation that the detergent environment did not introduce major artifacts.

results.result: Slc26a9T forms an elongated dimer (~100 Å × 50 Å) with STAS domains protruding 38 Å into the cytosol. The dimer interface is highly unusual, with only 11% of buried surface from transmembrane domain contacts, 16% from STAS-STAS contacts, and the remainder from swapped STAS-TMD interactions. The extended N-terminus binds to the STAS domain and contributes to dimer stability.
results.evaluation: Claims C56-C61 are directly supported by the cryo-EM structure and quantitative analysis of the dimer interface. The dimensions (C56-C57) are measured from the structure. The unusual nature of the interface (C58) is supported by comparison to other proteins with similar folds. The quantitative breakdown of buried surface areas (C59-C60) is calculated from the structure. The role of the N-terminus (C61) is observed structurally, though functional validation of its contribution to stability could strengthen this claim.

results.result: The STAS domains act as the primary platform for subunit interactions in the Slc26a9T dimer. The STAS domain structure closely resembles those from SLC26A5 (Prestin) and SLC26Dg, consisting of a six-stranded β-sheet core with four α-helices. Specific loop regions make contacts with the opposing TMD, and these contact residues are strongly conserved among family members. The removed IVS and CT regions would be positioned away from the dimer interface, available for interactions with accessory proteins.
results.evaluation: Claims C62-C69 are well-supported by the structural data and sequence analysis. The role of STAS domains as interaction platforms (C62) is directly observed and consistent with previous functional studies showing deleterious effects of STAS mutations. The structural similarity to other STAS domains (C63) validates the model. The specific contacts (C65) and their conservation (C66) are observed from the structure and sequence alignments. The inference about the location of removed regions (C69) is reasonable based on the truncated structure.

results.result: The transmembrane domain (TMD) conforms to a 7+7 inverted repeat topology with 14 membrane-inserted α-helices, segregated into a convex core module (α1-4, 9-11) carrying the ion-binding site and a concave gate module (α5-7, 12-14). The TMD shows high similarity to SLC26Dg (RMSD 2.0 Å). The structure represents an inward-open state, with a large cavity accessible from the intracellular side but no contiguous pore to the extracellular side.
results.evaluation: Claims C70-C76 are strongly supported by the structural data and comparison to related proteins. The topology (C70-C71) and domain organization (C72-C73) are directly observed in the structure. The similarity to SLC26Dg (C74) with RMSD of 2.0 Å indicates high structural conservation. The identification of an inward-open state (C76) is a reasonable inference from the structural features described in C75, though definitive assignment of conformational states typically benefits from multiple structures or additional functional data.

results.result: The nanodisc structure differs from the detergent structure in the conformation of the core module, which has rotated approximately 14° and moved 4 Å toward the extracellular side. This conformation likely represents an intermediate state on the transition toward an outward-facing state.
results.evaluation: Claims C77-C78 are supported by comparison of the two cryo-EM structures. The quantitative description of the conformational change (C77) is measured from the structural superposition. The interpretation as an intermediate state (C78) is a reasonable inference based on the direction and magnitude of the movement, though it remains an interpretation rather than a definitive assignment. The observation of different conformations in different environments strengthens the evidence for an alternate-access mechanism.

results.result: Slc26a9T has several distinguishing structural features compared to SLC26Dg: a loop-helix structure (α5') that fills a depression at the membrane boundary, an extended extracellular loop between α3-α4 containing predicted glycosylation sites, and a significantly longer N-terminus with scattered helical segments contacting the inner membrane leaflet. These features are likely preserved in mammalian SLC26 transporters due to high sequence conservation.
results.evaluation: Claims C79-C84 are well-supported by the structural data and sequence analysis. The specific structural features (C79-C83) are directly observed in the cryo-EM structure and clearly distinguished from the bacterial homolog. The prediction of glycosylation sites (C80) is supported by citation to a previous study. The inference that these features are preserved in other mammalian paralogs (C84) is reasonable based on sequence conservation, though direct structural confirmation would strengthen this claim.

results.result: In the inward-facing conformation, anions enter via a wide aqueous vestibule with positive electrostatic potential from basic residues. The linear I-V relationship of wild-type Slc26a9T is compatible with symmetric rate-limiting barriers. Charge-reversal mutations of basic residues near the binding site (K270E, K443E) cause outward rectification, indicating increased inward barriers, while mutations of extracellular basic residues (K221E, K431E) cause inward rectification.
results.evaluation: Claims C85-C90 are well-supported by the combination of structural analysis, electrostatic calculations, and mutagenesis data. The structural features and electrostatics (C85) are directly observed. The interpretation of the linear I-V relationship (C86) is supported by citations to previous work on similar systems. The mutagenesis results (C87-C90) provide strong functional validation of the structural observations and electrostatic calculations, demonstrating the importance of these residues for the transport mechanism.

results.result: An anion binding site is inferred to be located in a pocket of the core domain between the N-termini of α3 and α10, at the apex of the inward-open cavity. This location is equivalent to substrate-binding sites in related transporters. The pocket is smaller than in SLC26Dg due to F128 projecting into it. Residues F128, F92, and L391 contribute to the partly hydrophobic character, while Q88, S392, and T127 could stabilize dehydrated anions.
results.evaluation: Claims C91-C96 are supported by structural analysis and comparison to related transporters, though the binding site is inferred rather than directly observed (no Cl- density was resolved). The location (C91-C93) is reasonable based on comparison to structures of related transporters where substrate binding has been observed. The structural features of the pocket (C94-C96) are directly observed. However, the specific interactions with anions (C96) remain speculative without direct structural evidence of bound substrate. The subsequent mutagenesis data (C97-C102) provide strong functional support for these inferences.

results.result: Mutagenesis of binding-site residues alters transport properties: S392A shows inward rectification, F128A and Q88A show outward rectification, while F92A and L391A show minor perturbations. The Q88E mutant shows severely compromised transport. Changes in the permeability-conductivity relationship are most pronounced for S392A and F128A. No binding-site mutants showed major increases in HCO3- or SO42- permeability or evidence of coupled transport.
results.evaluation: Claims C97-C102 are strongly supported by comprehensive mutagenesis and electrophysiology data. The I-V relationships (C97-C98) and the effects on permeability and conductivity (C100-C101) are directly measured. The severe effect of Q88E (C99) is particularly informative, as it replaces a conserved residue with one found in prokaryotic transporters, providing insight into substrate selectivity. The negative result regarding HCO3- and SO42- permeability in mutants (C102) is important for understanding the determinants of substrate specificity.

results.result: The dimeric organization of Slc26a9 differs markedly from SLC4 and SLC23 family members, which interact via extended interfaces between gate modules. In Slc26a9, the TMD interface is minimal while subunit interactions are mediated by cytoplasmic STAS domains. Similar minimal TMD contacts were recently proposed for SLC26Dg and observed in the mechanosensitive channel OSCA.
results.evaluation: Claims C103-C106 are well-supported by structural comparison and citations to previous work. The differences from SLC4 and SLC23 families (C103) are directly observable from structural superposition. The description of the Slc26a9 interface (C104) is supported by the quantitative analysis of buried surface areas. The comparisons to SLC26Dg (C105) and OSCA (C106) appropriately contextualize the findings and show that while unusual, this type of oligomerization is not unprecedented.

results.result: Slc26a9 shows large uncoupled Cl- currents that saturate at high mM concentrations, properties consistent with a fast bidirectional uniport mechanism rather than a channel. The high Km matches intracellular Cl- concentration, fostering high turnover. Structural data suggest an alternate-access mechanism, with the inward-facing structure showing the binding site accessible to the cytoplasm and the intermediate conformation showing the site buried between core and gate modules. The core module makes ascending/descending rigid-body movements relative to the immobilized gate-STAS complex, resembling an elevator mechanism.
results.evaluation: Claims C107-C115 are well-supported by the combination of functional and structural data. The functional properties (C107) are confirmed by electrophysiology. The interpretation as a uniport mechanism (C108) is a reasonable inference from the data, though the distinction between a very fast transporter and a channel can be subtle. The structural evidence for an alternate-access mechanism (C111-C114) is strong, with two distinct conformations captured. The comparison to an elevator mechanism (C114-C115) is supported by citations and is consistent with the observed rigid-body movements.

results.result: Homology to the outward-facing structure of SLC4A1/Band 3 permits anticipation of the extent of conformational changes in Slc26a9, with basic residues likely creating a positive electrostatic environment in the extracellular vestibule. The role of electrostatics is supported by functional experiments and Poisson-Boltzmann calculations. During transport, Cl- is dragged across the transmembrane electric field, likely facilitating conformational changes. A similar mechanism may underlie electromotility in Prestin.
results.evaluation: Claims C116-C119 are supported by structural homology, electrostatic calculations, and mutagenesis data. The homology modeling (C116) is reasonable given the structural similarity to SLC4A1. The electrostatic calculations (C117) provide quantitative support for the proposed mechanism. The inference about Cl- movement facilitating conformational changes (C118) is reasonable based on the electrostatic properties. The speculation about Prestin (C119) is appropriately tentative and supported by citation, though it remains a hypothesis requiring further testing.

results.result: The inability of Slc26a9 to transport SO42- is likely related to insufficient binding site interactions for divalent anions, as the site lacks positive countercharges. Other mammalian SLC26 members have similar binding sites but contain a positively charged residue at the position equivalent to V393 in Slc26a9. The inability to transport HCO3- is remarkable given that NO3- is transported; this may be due to perturbation of the HCO3-/CO32- equilibrium at the binding site, with the positive electrostatic potential stabilizing the divalent CO32- form.
results.evaluation: Claims C120-C124 are supported by structural analysis, homology modeling, and functional data. The explanation for lack of SO42- transport (C120) is a reasonable inference from the binding site structure. The observation about other family members (C121-C122) is supported by sequence alignment and homology modeling. The explanation for lack of HCO3- transport (C123-C124) is more speculative, as it involves a hypothesis about protonation state changes at the binding site that is not directly tested. However, it is a plausible mechanistic explanation consistent with the observed selectivity.

results.result: High homology between mammalian SLC26 paralogs suggests a common architecture and similar conformational transitions. The diversity of functional phenotypes (uncoupled uniport, coupled exchange, motor activity) could rely on small localized structural differences imposing variable energy barriers. Uncoupled uniporters like Slc26a9 presumably have small barriers permitting unloaded transporter transitions, while coupled exchangers have increased binding affinity and enlarged barriers preventing unloaded transitions. The motor function of Prestin could result from an insurmountable barrier preventing the final transition to an outward-facing state.
results.evaluation: Claims C125-C130 are largely speculative, though based on reasonable mechanistic principles. The inference about common architecture (C125-C126) is supported by sequence conservation and the structural similarity to SLC26Dg. However, the mechanistic explanations for functional diversity (C127-C130) are hypotheses that, while plausible and consistent with the data, are not directly tested in this study. These claims represent interesting models for future investigation but should be considered speculative interpretations rather than established findings. Direct structural and functional characterization of other family members would be needed to test these hypotheses.

results.result: Electrophysiology experiments show instantaneous activity not obviously dependent on activating ligands. A potential activation mechanism could be mobilization from intracellular stores, possibly regulated by phosphorylation, consistent with the predominantly intracellular localization of full-length Slc26a9. The IVS may harbor modifiable motif elements involved in surface-trafficking regulation.
results.evaluation: Claims C131-C133 are speculative regarding regulation mechanisms. The observation of instantaneous activity (C131) is supported by the electrophysiology data. However, the proposed activation mechanisms (C132-C133) are hypotheses based on previous studies and the observed localization differences between full-length and truncated constructs. These are reasonable speculations that warrant further investigation, but they are not directly tested in this study. The authors appropriately note that these hypotheses must be evaluated in more physiologically relevant contexts.

results.result: SLC26A9 is found in lung and stomach epithelia where it mediates luminal electrogenic chloride transport, contributing to airway clearance and gastric acid production. It colocalizes with CFTR and has proposed regulatory interactions with CFTR. Knockout mice develop airway and gastrointestinal pathologies, and human polymorphisms correlate with altered severity of airway clearance disorders. SLC26A9 has been proposed as a therapeutic target for cystic fibrosis.
results.evaluation: Claims C1-C3 and C9-C14 summarize established knowledge from previous studies, all supported by appropriate citations. These claims provide important context for the current work but are not novel findings of this study. The citations appear appropriate and the statements accurately represent the current understanding of SLC26A9's physiological roles and therapeutic potential.

results.result: The SLC26 family consists of ten functional mammalian paralogs with distinct tissue targeting and transport mechanisms. SLC26A5 (Prestin) functions as a voltage-dependent motor protein rather than a transporter. The transport mode of SLC26A9 is controversial, with some reports showing Cl-/HCO3- exchange and others showing uncoupled Cl- conductance. Prior to this study, no high-resolution structures existed for eukaryotic SLC26 members, with structural information limited to the bacterial SLC26Dg. SLC26 transporters form functional oligomers, but the quaternary arrangement was unknown.
results.evaluation: Claims C15-C26 provide background information about the SLC26 family and the state of knowledge prior to this study. All claims are supported by appropriate citations to previous work. These claims accurately represent the field and establish the rationale for the current structural and functional studies. They are not novel findings but important context.

results.result: The cryo-EM structures define the general architecture of eukaryotic SLC26 family members and reveal an unusual mode of oligomerization relying predominantly on the STAS domain. The structures support a rapid alternate-access mechanism mediating uncoupled chloride transport with negligible bicarbonate or sulfate permeability. A selective anion binding site is located in the center of a mobile module within the transmembrane domain.
results.evaluation: Claims C4-C8 represent the major conclusions of the study, stated in the abstract. These are well-supported by the comprehensive structural and functional data presented in the manuscript. The structures (C4) are of sufficient quality to define the architecture. The unusual oligomerization mode (C5) is clearly demonstrated by the quantitative analysis of the dimer interface. The transport mechanism (C6-C7) is supported by both structural evidence (two conformations) and functional data (selectivity, kinetics). The binding site location (C8) is supported by structural analysis and extensive mutagenesis.
